Team — here's my read from running Orion's demand through our latency/cost simulator (see attached PDF). Key bullet points: 

- Short chat path (<= 512 tokens): L4 (8GB VRAM / accelerated INT8) is by far the most cost-efficient. We can achieve ~1200 tps at ~220ms p99 when packed with continuous batching and prefix cache.
- Long generation path (> 1k tokens): H100 (80GB) is required for native large-context inference without aggressive chunking. Using H100 gives lower memory pressure and simpler KV handling, p99 ~450ms for 1k+ streams but can be optimized with sequence-slicing to ~300–350ms.
- A100 (40GB) fits between: better than L4 for memory but weaker than H100 on transformer kernels for long sequences. A100 is a good compromise if Orion wants fewer SKUs but will need more nodes to hit throughput targets.

Operational tradeoffs:
- Memory growth: 10% long-run jobs will occupy ~30–40% of our H100 cluster capacity if provisioned only for long jobs; recommend a small H100 pool sized for concurrent long jobs with autoscale policy and spot-burst for transient peaks.
- Cost: blended per-token cost (estimate): L4 ~$0.004 / 1k tokens, A100 ~$0.018 / 1k tokens, H100 ~$0.032 / 1k tokens (reserved pricing assumptions).
- Fallbacks: configure smart routing: prefer L4 for short; route to A100 when L4 saturated; fall back to H100 only for long-context jobs or when we detect generation blow-up. This keeps tail latency constrained while optimizing spend.

Recommended 12-month phased fleet (pilot → steady):
1) Pilot (months 0–2): 20 L4 nodes + 2 A100 nodes; baseline autoscale, prefix cache warmup.
2) Phase 1 scale (months 3–6): 80 L4 + 6 A100 + 3 H100 (reserved) — covers expected peaks with 20% headroom.
3) Phase 2 (months 7–12): 200 L4 + 16 A100 + 8 H100 — for 2x growth. Keep options for reserved commit on H100 if long-run % stabilizes.

Operational notes: enable pre-warming for H100 scheduled jobs, configure metric-based canary for any model variant swaps, and include paging/eviction policy for KV cache to limit memory growth.

Attachments: sku_latency_model.pdf — simulation outputs and assumptions (token mix, batch sizes, kernel selections).
